content.text: Community members expressed frustration over perceived lack of communication from the ElizaOS team across multiple days. Users questioned whether the project was still active, noting the official X account had not posted since May, the chat was largely inactive, and the token price was hitting new all-time lows. Odilitime was specifically praised as the only team-adjacent member consistently providing accurate and respectful information. On July 5, Odilitime clarified that ElizaOS Labs was dissolved in April but the foundation remains active, open source contributors continue to help, and work on ElizaCloud is ongoing. Community members were directed to GitHub activity as evidence of continued development.

A discussion arose regarding a code change (issue #10732) that sets USDC as the default payout asset instead of the elizaOS token. A community member raised concerns that this could reduce elizaOS token utility and eliminate buybacks. Odilitime clarified that the change is specifically about payouts, not payments, and that paying out in elizaOS would likely cause businesses to dump the token, making USDC a safer option. Odilitime confirmed that elizaOS remains one of the accepted crypto tokens for payments, and that USDC payouts apply to the new cloud business services.

On July 5, a user asked whether ElizaOS is SOC 2 Type II certified and ready for enterprise use. Odilitime confirmed that ElizaCloud uses SOC 2 Type II certified providers. A community member also noted that the AI-ElizaOS-Updates channel has not been updated in a long time and requested someone address it.

GBLIN announced the release of plugin-gblin version 0.2.4 for Eliza agents. The update introduces a new action called GET_GBLIN_RISK_ATTESTATION, which allows an agent to pay $0.003 via x402 in USDC on Base gaslessly and receive a 10-minute EIP-712-signed proof of the current BTC/ETH risk regime. The proof can be attached to subsequent agent actions and verified by any counterparty for free. The plugin also includes treasury health checks, the ability to park idle USDC into an on-chain index, and JIT-swaps back to USDC for invoice payments, totaling 4 actions and 1 provider running against live Base mainnet.

In the coders channel, a developer shared a new plugin called cabal-hunter, built to address a gap in trading agents where on-chain wallet data is not considered. The plugin traces holder clusters and funding sources, flags bundled buys, serial rug deployers, and honeypot liquidity pools. It is available via npm as elizaos-plugin-cabal-hunter with the first 100 scans free. The developer requested feedback from others running trading agents on what additional signals would be useful before a buy decision.

In the coders channel, Schlegel introduced Paxeer Network, describing it as an EVM layer 1 blockchain built for agent commerce with native payment rails, 200ms block times, near instant finality, and low gas fees. The project claims to be chain agnostic through LayerX integration and positions itself as a settlement layer suited for eliza agents. Schlegel, identified as head of Public Relations and Integration, mentioned the project has been in development for 2.5 years and shared a developer tracker link. He expressed interest in connecting with the elizaOS community and stated they have built and tested an agent on their chain.

In the partners channel, a representative from DAPPCRAFT reached out to Odilitime requesting a 30-minute call to discuss a potential collaboration, noting that Bitfury is the lead investor in their project. Odilitime responded indicating they had already inquired about the matter but received no response and planned to follow up. Later in the week, DEMIAN from DAPPCRAFT also reached out to the jintern bot requesting assistance.

June 30 saw significant progress across voice infrastructure, agent orchestration, and build systems. Real-time wake-word detection was enabled via OpenWakeWordDetector, the desktop UI was streamlined by removing legacy stacks, and voice end-to-end testing was advanced with new Apple Stage-B STT benchmarks. The team hardened agent security by introducing read-only verifiers, sub-agent spend-cap warnings, and improved prompt-injection protections. Plugin builds were consolidated onto a shared driver for better type-safety, CI/CD pipelines were optimized for cloud reliability, and the plugin registry was expanded with the addition of elizaos-plugin-quantumscan and eliza-plugin-klymax402.

On July 1, the ElizaOS team focused on internationalization-friendly routing, embedded application security, and mobile and benchmark stability. Core actions including VISION, ALARM, MUSIC, PREDICTION_MARKET, and DOCUMENT were refactored to use structured operation parameters instead of English keyword regex, significantly improving internationalization support. The team also formalized a shortcut allow-list boundary for intent resolution to further harden the routing layer. On the security front, the embedded SPA bootstrap for the /embed endpoint was finalized, integrating Discord OAuth2 and session token validation. Production-grade fail-closed security guards were deployed for rate limiting and payout status checks.

Mobile stability saw meaningful progress with the implementation of real-device Android smoke tests covering touch gestures, sleep-wake cycles, and view-runtime soaking. Benchmark harnesses were also calibrated with reasoning-safe token budgets and real-Chromium browser testing to ensure reliable and accurate performance measurements. Several pull requests remain in progress, including fixes for cloud app structured confirmations, desktop icon inclusion, UI launcher audit stabilization, and a new PTY service plugin for an interactive CLI experience.
